questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the key difference in setup effort and payload between Change Data Capture (CDC) and Platform Events?
options: CDC requires designing a custom schema, while Platform Events require no setup at all
Both require exactly the same amount of setup effort and produce identical payloads

CDC is a built-in feed requiring no custom payload design, automatically streaming changed fields for enabled objects; Platform Events require designing a custom event schema, which costs more setup but allows a business-meaningful payload
Platform Events can only be used for deleting records, never for creates or updates
questions.explain: CDC is the faster, lower-effort option because it streams Salesforce's own record changes automatically. Platform Events cost more setup because you design the schema yourself, but that buys a custom payload useful when multiple systems need the same structured business event.

questions.q: Why is Bulk API 2.0's asynchronous, job-based design well suited for large data migrations rather than a limitation?
options: Because it processes exactly one record at a time, matching real-time use cases
Because Bulk API 2.0 cannot be used for mass updates, only for inserts
Because Bulk API 2.0 guarantees results return in the exact same order submitted
Because large volumes processed as a background job, with results reconciled afterward, avoid the fragility and limits that pushing that same volume through a real-time, synchronous path would hit
questions.explain: Bulk API 2.0 is designed for exactly the profile where 'a few minutes later' costs nothing real -- migrations, nightly syncs, mass updates -- and callers are expected to reconcile results that can come back in a different order than submitted.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a real risk of relying on a real-time integration pattern that a batch job's failure mode doesn't usually share?
options: A silently failing subscriber or expired replay window can quietly drop data with no obvious symptom, while a failed batch job typically leaves a clearer failure signal like a job status or row count mismatch
Real-time integrations always cost more in Salesforce licensing than batch jobs
Real-time integrations cannot be monitored at all
Batch jobs are not permitted to process more than 1,000 records
questions.explain: The lesson highlights that real-time pipelines can fail quietly in ways that are harder to notice without specialized event-driven monitoring, compared to a batch job's more visible failure signals.

questions.q: What default approach does this lesson recommend for choosing between real-time and batch integration?
options: Default to real-time for every integration because it sounds more sophisticated
Default to batch unless something specific about the business process requires real-time freshness
Always use Bulk API 2.0 regardless of data volume or freshness needs
Alternate between real-time and batch randomly to balance system load
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against reaching for real-time by default and recommends asking whether the business process on the other end can actually use that freshness before paying for the added fragility and monitoring burden.

questions.q: What capability do both Change Data Capture and Platform Events share that matters when a downstream subscriber goes offline temporarily?
options: Automatic deletion of all missed events after one minute
Automatic conversion of missed events into Bulk API 2.0 jobs
Replay, which lets a durable subscriber catch up on events it missed while offline
Neither CDC nor Platform Events support any form of replay
questions.explain: Both CDC and Platform Events support replay for durable subscribers, which is what lets a downstream system that was briefly offline catch up on events without permanently losing them.
